page.layout: One page of text in a single column, below a decorative woodcut border at the top. A centred Greek greeting line stands above a rule, followed by the section number "I." and the opening paragraph with a woodcut initial. No marginal notes. Printed signature "A 2" at the foot. The faint mirrored text in the right and left margins is show-through.

main_text.p: IUSTIFICATIO, Nomen ecclesia-sticae autoritatis & usus, Latinis est Probatio vel Appro-batio: Judicium & sententia, quâ Quis, vel Quid, pro justo habetur: Absolutio. Formatum à consimili Verbo, Ju-STIFICARE: quod Latini dicunt, Justum censere seu judica-re: Pro justo habere: Justum pronunciare: Absolvere.
Componitur ex Justus, & Facio, i.e. judico, reputo. Justus autem à Justitia, & haec à Jure denominationem habet.

§. 2. Graecis Δικαιώσις, prefsè-vertendo, Justatio appella-tur. A' Δικαιῶ, prefsè, Justo, as, are. Glos. Cyrill. exponit: Justifico, Æquum censeo. Vulgo tam de Re, quàm de Persona, capitur. Duo praecipuè denotat: Δίκαιον νομίζω, Justum reputo vel censeo: &, Κολάζω, Punio. Suid. Hesych. Phavor. Posteriore tamen significatu in S. Codice non usurpatur.
A' Δίκαιος Justus: quod à Δίκη descendit, id est: 1. Jus, Justitia, Meritum: 2. Dica, Lis, Judicium. 3. Poena, Supplicium.

Opponitur ei, tum Ἔγκλησις, quae & Κατηγορία, Accusatio: Luc. VI, 7. Joh. XVIII, 29. ab Ἐγκαλέω, In jus voco: tùm Κατάκρισις. Condemnatio. quae & Κατάκριμα, & simpliciter Κρῖμα, Judicium. Id quod aliàs Κρῖμα Θανάτυ, Judicium sive sententia mortis. Vid. Luc. XXIV, 20.
Perinde, Verbo Δικαιοῦσθαι opponitur Καταδικάζεσθαι, Condemnari: Matth. XII, 37. Idem valet, Καταχρίνεσθαι, Damnari: Matth. XXVII, 3. & absolutè sic ponitur, pro Κατα-

page.notes: Greek greeting line and several Greek words (Ἰ'ησ̃, Χεισ̃, Κατάκρισις, Κρῖμα, Θανάτυ, Καταχρίνεσθαι, Καταδικάζεσθαι) are doubtful in the scan and are marked [?] where uncertain; accents are not clearly legible. The woodcut initial is read as I. "Ju-STIFICARE" keeps the printed small capitals. The "2" at the top right corner looks like a later hand, not a printed page number, so no page_number is given. Printed "Glosf." read as "Glos." under the long-s rule. "Justatio" is copied as printed, possibly a misprint for Justificatio.
